Regeneration with an effect of conspecific adult density

Source: R/Processes.R
regeneration_adult_effect.Rd

A variant of regeneration_adult in which the density of conspecific adults is an EFFECT on recruitment rather than a gate: a species without adults on the site still recruits a share f0 of its potential, so bare ground can be colonised from an empty stand.

Usage

regeneration_adult_effect(
  species,
  parReg,
  pred,
  light,
  dbh = NULL,
  trees = NULL,
  debug = FALSE
)

Arguments

species

torch.Tensor species information.

parReg

torch.Tensor Regeneration parameters. 0 <= parReg <= 1 This parameter denotes the fraction of light needed for a species to regenerate. In general low values for high regeneration and high values for low regeneration.

pred

torch.Tensor Prediction values.

light

torch.Tensor Available light variable for calculation.

dbh

torch.Tensor cohort diameters, [sites, patches, cohorts].

trees

torch.Tensor stems per cohort, [sites, patches, cohorts].

debug

logical If TRUE, return the intermediate components as a list. Defaults to FALSE.

Value

torch.Tensor mean recruitment, stems ha^-1 step^-1, [sites, patches, species]. With debug = TRUE, a list that also holds adults (A, stems ha^-1, [sites, 1, species]), f0 and seed (f(A)).

Details

The conspecific adult density A_k (stems ha^-1) is computed as in regeneration_adult: the stems of species k weighted by a soft adult threshold sigmoid((d - x_k) / tau) (tau = 2 dbh units), pooled over the patches of the site. The adult term is $$f(A_k) = f_{0,k} + (1 - f_{0,k}) \frac{A_k}{A_k + A_{1/2,k}}$$ with \(f_0 = \mathrm{sigmoid}(\mathrm{reg\_adult\_logitf0}) \in (0, 1)\), and the mean recruitment is $$m = r(\mathrm{light}) \, e^{\mathrm{env}} f(A) + \mathrm{reg\_floor},$$ capped by the Beverton-Holt term of regeneration_capped, K m / (K + m).

f0 is the share of the potential recruitment a species gets on a site without conspecific adults – seed rain from outside the site, advance regeneration. It rises to 1 as adults become abundant. f0 -> 1 means no adult effect (the process becomes regeneration_capped); f0 -> 0 recovers the gate of regeneration_adult, where a species without adults recruits only at reg_floor.

The soft threshold counts small stems partly: a 1-cm stem is about 1.5 % of an adult at x = 9.4 cm, so a low A_half gives a non-zero adult term even in a stand of seedlings.

The cap reg_logK is created by finn() as for regeneration_capped (resolution from createProcess(cap = ), prior from prior/prior_lambda), so it need not be declared. Declare the three adult parameters with createProcess(custom_parameters = ); a length-1 init gives one shared value and a length-N_species init one value per species:

  • reg_adult_logx: the log adult threshold, x = exp(reg_adult_logx) in the units of dbh;

  • reg_adult_logA: the log half-saturation adult density, A_half = exp(reg_adult_logA) stems ha^-1;

  • reg_adult_logitf0: the logit of the share without adults, f0 = plogis(reg_adult_logitf0).

As for regeneration_adult, forward() passes dbh and trees because the signature has them. Called without dbh/trees (as the ALE code in xAI.R does), the function returns recruitment with the seed source present (f = 1).

See also

regeneration_adult, regeneration_capped, createProcess(), recruitment for the recruitment options and how to combine them

Examples

library(data.table)
# three sites of the bundled Oregon FIA sample (?fia_obs_dt)
sites <- 1:3
Nsp   <- max(fia_obs_dt$species)
init  <- makeInitCohorts(fia_init_trees[siteID %in% sites], Nspecies = Nsp)

FINN.seed(1)
m <- finn(
  N_species = Nsp, recruits_dbh = 12.9,
  regeneration_process = createProcess(
    ~ temp + prec, FINN::regeneration_adult_effect,
    custom_parameters = list(reg_adult_logx    = rep(log(20), Nsp),   # adult from 20 cm
                             reg_adult_logA    = rep(log(20), Nsp),   # half effect at 20 adults/ha
                             reg_adult_logitf0 = qlogis(0.2)),        # 20 % without adults, shared
    optimizeSpecies = TRUE, optimizeEnv = TRUE))
fit(m, data = fia_obs_dt[siteID %in% sites], env = fia_env_dt[siteID %in% sites],
    init_cohort = init, epochs = 2L, patches = 4, patch_size = 0.06, plot_progress = FALSE)
#> ℹ weights: intercept-only baseline x your vector (dbh=0.00243, ba=12, trees=0.968, growth=1.84e+04, mortality=38.5, regeneration=0.768)
#> ℹ share of the objective at the intercept-only baseline (scaled): dbh=17%, ba=17%, trees=17%, growth=17%, mortality=17%, regeneration=17%
# the fitted share of the potential recruitment without conspecific adults
plogis(as.numeric(m$reg_adult_logitf0))
#> [1] 0.1968171
